clue.text: Turncoat's new direction agreed

indicators.note: new tells us the letters are made into a fresh arrangement

parts.note: NE, north-east, is a compass direction

explanation.surface: A defector announces that a change of course has been settled on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' is the anagram signal. 'direction' supplies a two-letter compass point here, not a single letter. The 's after 'Turncoat' is just a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A renegade deserts their side for the enemy, exactly what a turncoat does.

clue.text: The more foolhardy having it for breakfast?

definitions.meaning: more reckless, the comparative of rash
something eaten at breakfast, a slice of bacon

explanation.walkthrough: The comparative of rash doubles as a strip of bacon eaten at breakfast.
explanation.definitionFit: Rasher is both the comparative of rash, meaning reckless, and a slice of bacon fried for the morning meal.

clue.text: Advanced from the north, approximately

parts.note: advanced, as in ahead of time, means early

explanation.surface: Troops pressed forward from the north, roughly speaking.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'from the north' suits N coming first, at the top.
explanation.definitionFit: Nearly means almost or roughly, the same as approximately.

clue.text: Girl taking a breather with boy

parts.note: a gill is the breathing organ of a fish
Ian is a boy's name

explanation.surface: A young woman takes a breather alongside a lad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a breather' is not a rest but something that breathes, a fish's gill.
explanation.definitionFit: Gillian is a female first name.

clue.text: Dined on last crust of bread, then fruit

indicators.note: last crust of tells us to take the end letter of the word bread

parts.note: dined means ate

explanation.surface: Someone finished the last crust of bread, then had some fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: A date is the sweet brown fruit of the date palm.

clue.text: A liniment not meant to be held in City Council's medical department

indicators.note: to be held in tells us the leftover letters sit inside the other pair of letters

parts.note: C is a standard abbreviation for city
C is a standard abbreviation for council

indicators.note: not tells us the letters of the word meant are taken out of A LINIMENT, in any order

explanation.surface: An ointment in a city council's health department is not meant to be kept.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' tells you to strike out the letters of the second word, in any order, from the first two; 'to be held in' then puts the remainder between the two Cs.
explanation.definitionFit: A clinic is a place or department in a hospital where patients get treatment.

clue.text: Physicians once hard to shake off?

definitions.meaning: people or things that cling on and will not let go

explanation.walkthrough: Leech was an old word for a doctor, and a leech is also the bloodsucker or hanger-on that clings.
explanation.definitionFit: Leech was archaic for a doctor, and leeches are clinging bloodsucking worms, so also persistent hangers-on.

clue.text: Ron is not travelling by rail in New Zealand -and one can't fly

definitions.text: rail in New Zealand -and one can't fly

indicators.note: travelling tells us the letters move about into a new order

explanation.surface: Ron won't go by train in New Zealand, and he cannot fly either.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rail' looks like the railway, but it is a family of birds; the takahe of New Zealand is a flightless rail.
explanation.definitionFit: Notornis is the genus name of the takahe, a large flightless bird of the rail family found in New Zealand.

clue.text: Plan a camping trip

indicators.note: trip suggests stumbling, so the letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone organises a camping holiday.
explanation.definitionFit: A campaign is an organised course of action aimed at a goal.

clue.text: Everything goes outside, in the allotment

indicators.note: outside tells us the attempts word wraps around the word for everything

parts.note: goes in the sense of attempts or tries means shots
everything means all

explanation.surface: Everything gets moved out of doors in the allotment garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'goes' is a noun here, as in 'have a few goes'; 'outside' tells you the attempts word wraps round the word for everything.
explanation.definitionFit: Shallots are small onions that gardeners commonly grow on vegetable plots.

clue.text: Rebuilding, must keep half of the dividing partition

indicators.note: rebuilding tells us the letters are put together in a new order
half of tells us to take only the back half of the word keep

explanation.surface: During rebuilding works, half of the interior wall has to stay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keep' looks like a container signal, but 'half of' takes its back half as letters; 'Rebuilding' then rearranges those with the word before.
explanation.definitionFit: A septum is a thin wall dividing two cavities, as between the nostrils.

clue.text: Dismiss from the parade?

parts.note: reads as ordering a soldier off the square, but the phrase is also the number of people who show up for the parade

explanation.walkthrough: To turn out is to expel, and the turnout is the crowd who come to a parade.
explanation.definitionFit: Turn out means expel or send away, and a turnout is the number attending an event.

clue.text: I recall removing last forkful, demolishing this cake

indicators.note: demolishing tells us the remaining letters are knocked down and rebuilt in another order
removing tells us a letter is taken out of the words I recall
last tells us to take the final letter of the word forkful

explanation.surface: Someone remembers polishing off the last mouthful of a pastry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'last' picks L from 'forkful'; 'removing' takes one L out of IRECALL, leaving IRECAL, which 'demolishing' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: An eclair is a long choux pastry filled with cream and topped with chocolate.

clue.text: In high spirits, a Europhile jigging —— but the French missed out

indicators.note: jigging, dancing about, tells us the letters are jumbled
missed out tells us those letters are removed from the word Europhile

parts.note: le is French for the

explanation.surface: A fan of Europe dances happily, but the French stay away from the celebration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missed out' strikes out the French article from the long word, and 'jigging' rearranges the remainder; the A goes on the end. 'In' just links.
explanation.definitionFit: Euphoria is a state of intense happiness and elation.

clue.text: Film-star in first Hollywood movie

indicators.note: movie here is read as move, telling us the letters shift into a new order
first tells us to take the opening letter of the word Hollywood

explanation.surface: A celebrity appears in their first Hollywood picture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Film' looks like a movie, but it means a thin dulling coat on metal. 'movie' rearranges STARIN to TARNIS; 'first' adds H from 'Hollywood'.
explanation.definitionFit: Tarnish is the dull coating that forms on silver and other metals.

clue.text: Removing all traces?

parts.note: reads as wiping away all evidence, but traces are the straps joining a horse to a cart, so it means taking the harness off

explanation.walkthrough: Traces are the side straps of a horse's harness; taking them all off is the literal meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking off a horse's harness means freeing it from its straps and traces, the gear that ties it to a cart.

clue.text: Toothless creature — ex-prime minister, heading for gallery

parts.note: Anthony Eden was a British prime minister in the 1950s
the Tate is a famous London art gallery

explanation.surface: A former prime minister with no teeth heads off to an art gallery.
explanation.definitionFit: Edentates are mammals such as sloths and anteaters that lack front teeth.

clue.text: Lover for Parisian has heart of a beast

indicators.note: has heart of tells us the French word holds the beast at its centre

parts.note: pour is French for for
a ram is a beast, a male sheep

explanation.surface: A Frenchman's lover is said to have the heart of an animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has heart of' puts A RAM in the middle of POUR, the French for 'for'.
explanation.definitionFit: A paramour is an illicit lover.

clue.text: Grave accent a help, maybe, in Latin?

definitions.text: Grave accent a help, maybe, in Latin?

parts.words: Grave accent a help, maybe, in Latin?
parts.note: grave suggests the accent mark but also means dead, and an accent is a way of speaking, so the clue hints at a tongue no longer spoken

explanation.walkthrough: Grave can mean dead, and accent suggests a tongue; Latin is the classic example of one no longer spoken.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin is the standard example of a tongue that no community now speaks natively.

clue.text: Thrash Manitoba in the final

annotationWithheld.why: Thrash Manitoba in the final (7): MB inside LAST gives LAMBST; the second A of LAMBAST has no source in the clue as held, so a word may be missing

clue.text: In space there's many a trick of the light

indicators.note: In tells us the bridge term goes inside the word for space

parts.note: a space is a gap
in bridge, a slam is winning all or all but one of the tricks

explanation.surface: Out in space there are plenty of optical illusions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'many a trick' is bridge talk: a slam wins all the tricks, or all but one. It looks like light playing tricks.
explanation.definitionFit: A gaslamp is a lamp that burns gas to give light.

clue.text: Not as bad, though he will take risks

definitions.meaning: someone who gambles, one who bets

explanation.walkthrough: One word means improved and also someone who places a bet.
explanation.definitionFit: Better is the comparative of good, and a better is a gambler who places wagers.

clue.text: Bird thus takes flight from quarry

indicators.note: takes flight suggests flying back, so the word thus is reversed

parts.note: so means thus
quarry, the hunted animal, is prey

explanation.surface: A bird flies off, escaping from its hunted target.
explanation.walkthrough: 'takes flight' turns the little word round, as if flying back; 'quarry' is the hunted animal, not a pit.
explanation.definitionFit: The osprey is a fish-eating bird of prey.

clue.text: Almost hitting the target with the girl next door?

parts.note: next door means near
a girl may be called miss

explanation.surface: Fancying the young woman living next door, someone almost scores.
explanation.definitionFit: A near miss is a shot that comes close to its target without striking it.

clue.text: Estimate number of donkeys on sea front

parts.note: a number of donkeys are asses

indicators.note: front tells us to take the first letter of the word sea

explanation.surface: Someone guesses how many donkeys are on the seafront.
explanation.walkthrough: 'front' gives S, the first letter of 'sea'. 'Sea front' reads as one place, but it is split.
explanation.definitionFit: To assess is to judge or evaluate the size or value of something.

clue.text: Staff of a thousand and one

parts.note: M is the Roman numeral for a thousand
an ace counts as one in cards

explanation.surface: Employees numbering a thousand and one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Staff' looks like employees, but it means a ceremonial rod.
explanation.definitionFit: A mace is a ceremonial staff carried as a symbol of authority.

clue.text: Admission for Oval was almost free

indicators.note: free here means loose, signalling the letters are rearranged
almost tells us the word was loses its final letter

explanation.surface: Entry to the Oval cricket ground used to be nearly free of charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' cuts WAS to WA; 'free' then rearranges OVAL plus WA. The Oval is a London cricket ground, which makes 'Admission' read as an entry fee.
explanation.definitionFit: An avowal is an open declaration or confession of something.

clue.text: Tin with flower on is for smoker's tobacco

parts.note: a tin is a can
an aster is a daisy-like flower

explanation.surface: A tin with a flower on the lid is for keeping a pipe smoker's tobacco.
explanation.definitionFit: Canaster is a coarse dried leaf, originally sold in rush baskets, smoked in pipes.

clue.text: Mistakes of sailor taken back in time

indicators.note: in tells us the turned sailor goes inside the word for time

parts.note: an era is a period of time

indicators.note: taken back tells us the sailor word is read from right to left

parts.note: a tar is a sailor

explanation.surface: The sailor's errors are recalled from an earlier period.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken back' turns the sailor round, and 'in' places him inside the period of time.
explanation.definitionFit: Errata are errors, especially those listed for correction in a printed book.

clue.text: Separate, yet comes back, outside, for afternoon get-together

indicators.note: outside tells us the turned word goes around the word for separate
comes back tells us the word yet is read from right to left

parts.note: separate means apart

explanation.surface: A couple split up, yet one returns for an afternoon gathering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'comes back' turns the three-letter word round; 'outside' puts that around the word meaning separate.
explanation.definitionFit: A tea party is a social gathering in the afternoon where tea is served.
